body: Fortnite is continuing the tradition of special Saturday hourly events during the Chapter 7 mini season, though this time they're treasure hours, centered around the pirate-themed "Treasure Hunters" season. During these hours, certain sprites will get increased drop rates, and you'll drop into the game with special items.

This week features Fortune treasure hours, increasing the drop rate for Fortune variant sprites. You'll also start the game with A$AP Rocky's Shock Rocket and a Self-Revive Kit. Fortune sprites will occasionally set off a radar-like effect, highlighting nearby chests — making them the perfect sprite to use to hunt down the Pirate Shop Access Token.

Notably, Epic Games has confirmed via X that drop rates for treasure (including the Pirate Shop Access Token) increase during these treasure hours. The drop rate for the token is usually 1 in 137,500, but during the treasure hours, there's a 1.5x chance of finding it. For the second treasure hour beginning at 9 p.m. EST, the token will be boosted to a 2x chance of finding it.

articles.headline: RPI football beats Ithaca, earns 1st berth in NCAA playoffs since 2021
keyFacts: The RPI football team defeated Ithaca 14-10 on Saturday to secure the program's first NCAA Division III playoff berth since 2021.
Senior tight end Grayson Hunter contributed two touchdown catches for RPI, helping overcome Ithaca and earn the Liberty League's automatic bid.
RPI can win the league title outright by defeating Union College in their next game on Saturday.
body: RPI quarterback Justin McCormcak jumps through a hole during a game against Hobart on Sept. 26 in Troy. (Jim Franco/Times Union)
Senior tight end Grayson Hunter caught two touchdown passes as the RPI football team edged host Ithaca 14-10 on Saturday to earn the program's first trip to the NCAA Division III playoffs since 2021.

The Engineers (7-2 overall, 6-0 Liberty League) won their sixth straight game to secure at least a share of the title with Ithaca (7-2, 6-1). RPI gets the Liberty League's automatic bid to the NCAAs because of the head-to-head tiebreaker.

"It's huge," RPI coach Ralph Isernia said. "It's something we've been working for, especially with this senior group the last four years. The time in the weight room and the time on the practice field, time in film meetings, all that stuff."
RPI, which snapped a four-game losing streak against Ithaca, can win the league outright by beating Union College for the Dutchman Shoes Trophy in Troy next Saturday.
Hunter, a backup behind starter Josh Young, made a diving 15-yard touchdown catch from starting quarterback Micah Balzarini for a 7-7 tie with 1:16 left in the second quarter.
With 4:22 left in the third quarter, Hunter caught a 19-yard pass from backup quarterback Justin McCormack on a ball that was tipped by an Ithaca defender to put RPI ahead 14-10.
"Certainly, there's a lot of attention that goes to Josh Young, and that's understandable," Isernia said. "But (Hunter) is able to get open and he's made plays for us this entire year."
Isernia said McCormack came into the game for Balzarini by design.
"Obviously, he brings another dimension with the run game and he's also an extremely effective passer as well," Isernia said.

RPI's defense held Ithaca well below its league-leading average of 40.3 points per game. Defensive linemen Owen Boland and Cameron Keeperman combined on a sack of quarterback Michael Reed that helped stop a late Bombers drive.
On the game's final play, Ithaca threw a Hail Mary pass from the RPI 48 that fell incomplete in a crowd in the end zone. RPI's Aidan Bekkenhuis was credited with the breakup.

articles.headline: The pros and cons of using an Amazfit smartwatch
keyFacts: Amazfit smartwatches offer affordable prices, long battery life, cross-device compatibility, and extensive health tracking features.
Limitations include a proprietary operating system with restricted app access, limited storage, and software support lasting only three years.
Engadget reports that users trade advanced app ecosystems for lower costs and reliable fitness tracking.
body: The pros and cons of using an Amazfit smartwatch
Amazfit watches are easy on your wallet, but they can’t do everything.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Amazfit smartwatches are widely considered to be good alternatives to the bigger brands. They're generally cheaper, with some models like the well-reviewed Amazfit Bip 6 available for as little as $80. But as you would expect, there are concessions to be made to justify the lower price.

The line from the Chinese company Zepp Health includes a wide range of smartwatches to suit any lifestyle, from casual wearers to serious athletes. However, they run on a proprietary OS that limits app access, and some models have limited storage. The companion app also isn't the most intuitive.

On the plus side, Amazfit smartwatches focus on AI-powered software using its Zepp Coach and offer long battery life, with some models lasting for up to 25 days per charge. You can also find deals on Amazfit smartwatches, which are already affordable to begin with.
Before you commit, it helps to know what you're getting and what you're giving up. Here's why so many people consider Amazfit in the first place.
Why Amazfit smartwatches are worth considering

Amazfit smartwatches are sleek, with designs that resemble other popular models. You'll find square-shaped options like the Bip 6 and Active 2 (Square) that look like an Apple Watch. There are also round-faced ones like the Amazfit Active Max and the Amazfit T-Rex 3, which is designed for outdoor adventurers and resembles a Garmin watch in its aesthetic.

Another advantage is cross-device compatibility. You can pair an Amazfit smartwatch with either iPhone or Android since it uses its own operating system and isn't tied to either. Many trusted outlets also rank Amazfit watch models among the best budget smartwatches, citing accurate health tracking along with their stylish designs. They also note that integrations like the AI Coach, Bluetooth calling and Alexa command support are top-notch.

Amazfit smartwatches also offer over 100 sports modes, from strength training and running to gardening and Tai Chi. And they have all the important sensors you'd want for data, including heart rate, sleep, temperature, GPS and more.

Amazfit is a solid budget smartwatch brand you can continue to use even if you swap phone platforms. There's also no subscription tier for any of the data it tracks and reports, and these watches are a step up from the best cheap fitness trackers, with larger screens for at-a-glance information and control on your wrist.
Amazfit smartwatches are not without downsides

Amazfit smartwatches run on the proprietary Zepp OS, so you can't access third-party apps the way you can with Wear OS watches. Instead, you're limited to a few productivity apps and games from the Zepp Store. The watches do integrate with third-party platforms like Strava, TrainingPeaks, Komoot and Runna, but you can't access Google Wallet, Google Maps, Uber, Starbucks, Gmail or banking apps. There's no Spotify app either, though you can listen on your phone and use the watch to control playback or use a remote app to mirror Spotify on the device.

Beyond apps, the software isn't as intuitive as others or as easy to navigate as those of better-known brands. You'll see unfamiliar terms like PAI, Amazfit's personal activity score and Biocharge, which is basically its equivalent of a readiness score. Some models have limited storage, which could cause issues with storing workout data or apps. The Amazfit Bip 6, for example, has 512MB of storage.

On longevity, Amazfit offers only three years of software and security support for its smartwatches. They won't stop working after that point, but it's worth factoring into the decision if you plan to hold onto the smartwatch for a while.

For a more intuitive experience with better app support, you might prefer going with affordable models from brands like Fitbit and Garmin instead, or even an older-model Samsung Galaxy Watch or Apple Watch, even if they're in their last years of software support. While Amazfit smartwatches aren't the best smartwatches you can buy, you will get reliable health tracking, long battery life and sleek designs for a great price, with a few caveats you might be able to live with.

articles.headline: Can Verstappen, Hamilton come from the back in Sao Paulo 'reverse grid' race?
keyFacts: Lando Norris starts on pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix alongside new world champion Kimi Antonelli.
Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start at the back of the grid due to power unit changes.
The race takes place on Sunday at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, with a high chance of rain forecast.
body: Sao Paulo GP: Can Max Verstappen, Lewis Hamilton come from the back again as Lando Norris hopes for rain to fight Kimi Antonelli

Lando Norris starts on pole in Brazil from Kimi Antonelli but there will be plenty of attention further down the field with Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton starting at the back; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm
Saturday 7 November 2026 23:26, UK
A mixed up grid and rain on the forecast has set up the prospect of a thrilling Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Sunday.
For the third year in a row, Lando Norris will start on pole position in Brazil with new F1 world champion Kimi Antonelli alongside him on the front row.

Unusually though, there will be plenty of attention further down the field as power unit changes for Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton mean they start at the back, while Ferrari's Charles Leclerc starts 14th for a 10-grid place penalty.

And Mercedes' George Russell, who was left frustrated to not qualify first after a strategic error from the team, starts seventh following a five-place grid penalty for a new internal combustion engine, so several of F1's biggest names will begin the Sao Paulo Grand Prix - lights out at 5pm on Sunday with build-up from 3.30pm, live on Sky Sports F1 - out of position.
"It's almost a reverse grid race, no?" Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports F1.
"Yeah, exciting. I think we want to lock in the points for the Constructors' Championship. But it's all floodgates open, the better. Let's race."
How far can Verstappen and Hamilton climb up the field?
Verstappen is no stranger to making his way through the pack at Interlagos after his remarkable victory from 17th in 2024 in the rain.
The Red Bull driver, who has won three times in Brazil, gained 11 places in the opening 11 laps before making the right strategy call to take a crucial victory.
Last year, Verstappen started from the pit lane and impressively charged his way to the podium in dry conditions, but he thinks it will be more difficult to get towards the front this time around.

"It's going to be a bit harder to overtake. The Overtake Mode doesn't really do a lot around here. Everyone is draining their battery from the last corner to Turn 1. Everyone has their wings open, so the effect is less than normal," he told Sky Sports F1.
"That will make it a bit harder to overtake once you get to the cars that are similar on lap times. The first few cars are not a problem. The others will be a little harder."
Hamilton memorably went from 20th to fifth in the 2021 Sprint in Brazil, after he was disqualified from Qualifying, then won the Grand Prix after starting 10th.
However, Hamilton will not have the same car advantage from five years ago with Ferrari struggling this weekend compared to their recent form.

But, the high chance of rain means Hamilton, and Verstappen, will have the chance to showcase their extraordinary skill and could still find themselves towards the pointy end of the field with a special performance.
"It will be tricky conditions but I love racing in the rain," said Hamilton.
"I was basically using the qualifying as a test to make sure the engine is working, and making sure the car felt good. I feel good for tomorrow."
Leclerc has less cars to overtake from 14th and feels he learned a lot from the wet qualifying by experimenting with set-up tweaks which will benefit him in the race.
"It's going to be very tricky. My biggest strength in the junior categories has been wet driving. Since my nine years with Ferrari, we have never found a way around it," he told Sky Sports F1.
"I still believe if we manage to find the right window of this car, we can fight for much better than top six."
Norris hoping for 'dark, gloomy day' to fight Antonelli

Perhaps quite fittingly, last year's F1 world champion Norris will start on pole from the new world champion Antonelli in the first race since the latter secured this year's title a week ago in Mexico.
McLaren have brought a new front wing, rear wing, beam wing and floor elements to their car this weekend and it appears to have made an immediate performance impact.
Norris and Antonelli traded lap times throughout Friday's practice sessions in the dry but the McLaren driver feels he needs rain to beat Antonelli on Sunday.
"I expect a battle no matter what. If it's dry, I probably expect a bigger battle because I don't think we quite have the speed compared to them," he told Sky Sports F1.

"That's why I feel like we had a very good day today. We made the most of conditions where it's not so much about who has the best car, it's more who can push things to the limit and make the most of that opportunity.
"I'm hoping when I wake up it's a dark, gloomy day because we will have a better chance then."
Norris pointed to Antonelli's impressive long run pace in the dry on Friday as the reason he's hoping for rain, whereas the Mercedes driver says he's open to any conditions.
"Hopefully, we can get off the line well, and let's see if it's going to be wet or dry," said Antonelli.
"In the dry, I felt very good over a single lap and on the long run, especially in FP2. So let's see. I'm looking forward to it.
Mercedes have a big opportunity to win the Constructors' Championship with Antonelli starting in second and Russell in seventh, while the two Ferraris are outside of the top 13.

If Mercedes outscore Ferrari by three points, or more, they will seal their ninth title since 2014 but the result of the race itself appears to be more important to the drivers, and Russell is hoping for more rain following his impressive qualifying.
"I felt really confident in the rain. I think my pace, along with Lando's, was by far the best out there," he said
"In the rain here, it's always a challenge. I hope it is wet. I feel I've got a greater chance if it's wet."

articles.headline: Zuffa Boxing 12 results, highlights: Cheavon Clarke stops Chris Billam-Smith, Da'Mazion Vanhouter shines again
keyFacts: Cheavon Clarke defeated Chris Billam-Smith by a seventh-round technical knockout during the main event of Zuffa Boxing 12 in London.
Denzel Bentley claimed a unanimous decision victory over Shane Mosley Jr. in his Zuffa debut after surviving a competitive 10-round bout.
Da'Mazion Vanhouter secured a first-round knockout against Ivan Balaz, and UFC president Dana White said he hopes to book Vanhouter again on December 11.
body: After twice scoring upset decisions over former cruiserweight champion Chris Billam-Smith in their amateur days, former British Olympian Cheavon Clarke added an upset stoppage victory Saturday over his rival in the pro ranks at Zuffa Boxing 12.

Clarke (13-2, 10 KOs), a native of Jamaica who trains out of the U.K., took out the nearly 5-to-1 betting favorite in Billam-Smith (22-3, 14 KOs) during the main event of the Zuffa-promoted card inside Copper Box Arena in London. Nicknamed "C4," Clarke twice dropped Billam-Smith in the seventh round before referee Lee Every stopped the bout at 1:24 of the round while CBS was pinned against the ropes.

Billam-Smith, a 36-year-old from the United Kingdom, lost a pair of 2016 amateur bouts to Clarke, including in the final of the British national championships and later that year in the English Title Series.

"It has been 10 years, but I don't have no beef with Chris," Clarke said. "He has been the world champion, so give him his credit. I'm not going to be someone I'm not [and disrespect him]. Shout out to Chris."

After Billam-Smith lost his WBO cruiserweight title via decision to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024, he won his next two fights, including an all-action slugfest with Ryan Rozicki in June that marked his Zuffa debut as "CBS" scored a 7th-round TKO.

The fight against Clarke, 35, was physical from the jump, with both boxers looking to establish themselves on the inside, which led to a series of clinching throughout the first half of the scheduled 10-round bout.
Billam-Smith began to work the body aggressively before Clarke turned the momentum in his direction in Round 5 when he worked from long distance and hurt CBS with a clean right cross.

"[Billam-Smith] is a strong guy," Clarke said. "Look, he's bigger than me. Most of these guys are bullying me, but I've never been bullied. My mom wouldn't have condoned it, so there you go.
"I don't need to prove anyone right other than myself. I believe in me and believe in my team," Clarke said. "I don't believe anybody trains as hard as me. They can try, but they don't."

Clarke opened Round 7 by scoring a clean knockdown on another right hand. Billam-Smith regained his feet but went down a second time on another right hand. Even though "CBS" regained his feet, his legs began to wobble and Clarke let his hands go enough to force the stoppage.

"I'm fine, it was a good shot, obviously," Billam-Smith said. "I made a mistake, but I felt like I was winning the fight, but fair play to Shep. We have had three fights and he has won them all, but I would love to run it back and get him eventually."
Clarke won his third straight fight since dropping a pair of decisions to Leonardo Mosquea and Viddal Riley. In June, on the CBS-Rozicki undercard, Clarke stopped Jack Massey in a 7th-round TKO.
Former middleweight titleholder Denzel Bentley wins Zuffa debut

Bentley, who was stripped of his WBO middleweight title late last month after signing on for his Zuffa Boxing debut, held off a gritty effort by veteran Shane Mosley Jr. to claim a unanimous decision on scores of 96-93, 95-94 and 96-94 over a competitive 10 rounds.

Mosley (23-6, 13 KOs), the 35-year-old son of Hall-of-Famer Shane Mosley Sr., got up from a crushing right hand that dropped him in Round 2 and survived a further barrage of punches to work his way back during the same round.
"I cracked [Mosley's chin], but he got up," Bentley said. "I thought he was gone. I thought if I put a lot of shots on him, he wouldn't hold up, but he came back."

Bentley (23-3-1, 18 KOs), a 31-year-old who was fighting in his home city, held Mosley off down the stretch and, after the win, called for a shot at Carlos Adames, the WBC middleweight title who makes his Zuffa debut next week in Saudi Arabia, or a showdown against Conor Benn, who was seated ringside.

"I was fighting more than just Shane Mosley Jr. out here; I felt like I was fighting the whole of boxing for some of the decisions I had recently made," Bentley said. "It would've been even sweeter if the belt was on the line and I could've defended my title."
Young heavyweight Da'Mazion Vanhouter continues red-hot start with knockout

At just 21 and appearing on his fourth Zuffa card of 2026, Vanhouter (14-0, 11 KOs) remained unbeaten with a first-round knockout of Ivan Balaz (9-2, 7 KOs). Vanhouter recorded a trio of knockdowns – all on body shots – before the fight was stopped at 2:04 by referee Kieran McCann.

Vanhouter scored his eighth consecutive knockout since a 2024 split-decision win over Cristian Rodriguez and improved to 4-0 with four stoppages inside of three rounds since signing with Zuffa Boxing.

After the fight, UFC president and CEO Dana White, who ringside in London, said he hoped to bring Vanhouter back for a fifth fight this year on Dec. 11 in Wales on the undercard of the long-awaited British heavyweight clash between former champions Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

articles.headline: Staten Island bucks Dems’ blue tsunami, rejects ‘one-party rule’ with re-election of Nicole Malliotakis
keyFacts: Republican Representative Nicole Malliotakis won re-election to Congress representing Staten Island and a portion of Brooklyn.
Staten Island Republicans also retained five state legislative seats and won a state judgeship during Tuesday's election.
Malliotakis credited the wins to Staten Island voters opposing Democratic policies in city and state government.
body: Unlike the rest of NYC and much of the US, Staten Island Republican candidates survived Election Day’s blue tsunami, where the GOP lost control of both chambers of Congress and Democrats expanded their dominance of the state Legislature by 14 seats.

Rep. Nicole Malliotakis handily won her fourth term in Congress despite getting snubbed for the first time by the local newspaper, the Staten Island Advance, which endorsed Democrat Mike Decillis — who lives in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn — over her support of President Trump. The seat represents all of Staten Island and a sliver of Brooklyn, including Bay Ridge.

“[Staten Island] voters are angry,” Malliotakis said. “We don’t like the one-party rule in the city and state, and we know who is to blame for the quality-of-life issues we’re facing, and that’s why we take it out on the Democrats.

NYC’s lone Republican in Congress, Malliotakis credited Staten Islanders for coming out in full force to support borough Republicans, saying they’re sick of being slammed by congestion pricing and tolls, saddled with soft-on-crime policies pushed by lefty Dems and paying disproportionately higher property taxes than other boroughs.

“We’re the smallest borough, so if you have little say in statewide elections and citywide elections, and you’re going to get stuck with a mayor and a governor you don’t like, at least we can elect people on the local level and have some control in pushing back against a radical agenda that is so out of touch with Staten Island,” she said.

Staten Island Republicans also retained three state Assembly and two Senate seats and even picked up a state judgeship. The winners included Assemblyman Michael Tannousis, the Staten Island Republican Party chairman.

That’s a far cry from nearby southern Brooklyn across the Verrazzano–Narrows Bridge, where Republicans lost four state Legislature seats in Tuesday’s election after making big strides in recent years.
Gov. Kathy Hochul, Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli and Attorney General Letitia James — all Democrats — easily won their re-election bids despite losing Staten Island.

And five ballot questions pushed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration –- which exponentially increase the socialist pol’s power under the guise of streamlining government — were overwhelmingly approved despite also being rejected by Staten Island voters.
Democrats slightly outnumber Republicans in the city’s most conservative borough, but voters there typically back Republicans at the polls and many support Staten Island breaking away from NYC.
Council Minority Leader David Carr, a Staten Island Republican, credited a strong borough GOP ticket led by Malliotakis for getting people out to vote.
“Even our middle-of-the-road voters are common-sense voters,” said Carr. “I’m not surprised that we weathered the storm, but I am surprised at the depth of [Republican] losses nationally.”

articles.headline: NFL trade rumors tracker: Live updates on news for Jonathan Taylor, Jacoby Brissett and more before 2026 deadline
keyFacts: Several NFL teams have completed trades and evaluated roster changes ahead of the November trade deadline.
The Indianapolis Colts have received multiple trade inquiries regarding running back Jonathan Taylor and quarterback Daniel Jones.
Reporters have tracked numerous trade discussions involving players across the league, including Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett.
body: JUMP TO:
NFL trade season started early, as Jeffery Simmons, Marvin Harrison Jr., Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner all found themselves on the move well in advance of the Nov. 10 deadline.
As the final buzzer approaches, though, contenders are looking to best position themselves to make a run.

The top name on the market might be Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, who told the team he doesn't want to be traded but might not have much of a choice as Indianapolis' season spirals. Other teams, including the Cowboys and Eagles, have interesting decisions to make on their path forward as they weigh whether to trade stars.
The Sporting News is tracking live updates on the latest NFL trade rumors ahead of the 2026 deadline. Follow along below with the news.

— Oct. 29: The Tennessee Titans traded DT Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chicago Bears for two first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-round pick.

Colts declining Daniel Jones inquiries
Nov. 7 — While the Colts have received calls about Daniel Jones, Tom Pelissero reports that so far, Indianapolis has "told interested teams they aren’t trading him."
Broncos consider making audacious move for Cardinals star Trey McBride

Nov. 7 — ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Denver checked in on McBride, a Fort Morgan, Colorado native who starred at Colorado State. The Cardinals summarily declined the proposal, proclaiming they had no interest in letting their star man go.
Multiple teams have inquired about Daniel Jones’ availability, per report

Nov. 7 — Jones is the latest in a string of Colts players to garner trade deadline interest, with NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reporting that Indianapolis had received multiple calls regarding its QB’s availability.
Derrick Henry could be on the move after Ravens' blowout loss

Nov. 6 —Henry, who is a free agent after the season, was frustrated by Baltimore's fourth straight loss on Thursday night in the Ravens' last game before the trade deadline. With Baltimore facing most of the season without Lamar Jackson, the team could decide to get draft capital back for Henry instead of keeping him for the remainder of the season.
Conflicting reports over Giants' willingness to play ball with Colts for Jonathan Taylor

Nov. 5 — Taylor remains the name on the lips of decision-makers ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, with SNY's Connor Hughes reporting that sources not connected to the Giants are unsure of whether New York will attempt to make a move for the Colts standout. Some believe head coach John Harbaugh wants to move aggressively to land the former Offensive Player of the Year winner. Others believe Indianapolis' asking price will prove too cost-prohibitive for the Giants — or any other side — to seek out his services.
Colts to wait until after Week 9 before exploring trades for Jonathan Taylor, others

Nov. 5 — The Colts have been monitoring interest in a series of players, headlined by Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs. However, according to insider Jordan Schultz, Indianapolis doesn't plan on making a move until after its Week 9 game vs. the Cowboys. It appears that if teams want to strike a deal with the Colts, they'll have to work quickly on Monday and Tuesday.
Ravens acquiring Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals

Nov. 4 — The Ravens are finalizing a deal to acquire QB Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports, though it won't be completed in time for Brissett to join the team before Thursday's game. Compensation has not yet been reported.
Colts' asking price for Taylor remains high

Nov. 4 — The Colts are still asking for a first-round pick for Jonathan Taylor and maintaining that they don't have to trade him, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports, while suitors believe a second-round pick plus another asset should be enough.
Teams 'have their eye' on Jets

articles.headline: One of the buggiest D&D games ever released, Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor, is back and actually playable again
keyFacts: SNEG released a new, functioning version of the 2001 Dungeons and Dragons game Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor on Steam and GOG.
The 2001 original release was widely criticized for severe bugs, including some that corrupted game files or deleted system files during uninstallation.
The rereleased game features technical upgrades like widescreen support, adjustable combat speed, controller support, and sharpened visuals without the original bugs.
body: "Not since the infamous debut of Daikatana has the release of a single game generated so much incensed indignation from early buyers." Our review of Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor didn't hold back. The 2001 dungeon crawler contained, our review said, "A multitude of outrageous bugs," including ones that corrupted saves, made quest items disappear, and most infamously deleted system files when you uninstalled the game.

SNEG's rerelease, available now on Steam and GOG, doesn't have those issues. It adds widescreen, controller support, adjustable combat speed, tooltips, an action bar, and sharpened visuals. If, like me, you skipped this one back in the day because of its reputation for being a hassle to play—even with the eventual patches and community fixes—now it's smooth and problem-free. I've played the opening hours without a single key item vanishing or save file going corrupt.

Don't get the wrong idea, though. Ruins of Myth Drannor isn't Vampire: The Masquerade – Bloodlines. This isn't an RPG masterpiece held back by its buggy release. It's a simplistic turn-based dungeon crawl that's mostly notable for being a spiritual successor to the first Gold Box D&D game, Pool of Radiance, and for adapting the then-new third edition of D&D's rules.

The 3.0 rules were a huge step forward at the time. Any character could choose any class, and Armor Class went up instead of down—you can't imagine how much of a drag it was explaining to new players that lower AC was better than high AC, and ideally you wanted a negative number. It also formalized the central mechanic of rolling a d20 and adding a number to beat a difficulty score. If you've played 5th edition, you'll recognize a lot of its DNA here.

Which is why it's a shame Ruins of Myth Drannor isn't a complete adaptation of those rules. You can't play a wizard—sorcerer is the only option for arcane casters—or a halfling or a gnome. You choose which class to improve when you advance a level, but don't get to decide where your skill points go or what feats to take. A couple of years later, The Temple of Elemental Evil would adapt the 3.5 rules update much more fully. Ruins of Myth Drannor feels rudimentary by comparison.

It's also not much of a story. Set 10 years after the events of Pool of Radiance, a new magical pool has opened in the ruined elven city of Myth Drannor so the evil sorceress and dracolich on the box art can get up to some shenanigans, and Elminster has sent a party of adventurers in to stop them. There's one fun twist to this otherwise bog-standard plot, and it's that you're not that first party of adventurers. You're the B-team sent as backup, but a magic portal mishap means you arrive too late to save the A-team and have to take on their quest.

Which explains why four level-one nobodies now have to clear out hundreds of orcs and skeletons from samey dungeon rooms. It's a slow-paced slog, especially in Myth Drannor's main halls, earning a drip-feed of experience points and gold coins from zombies and ghouls, hoping an orc doesn't score a crit and drop one of your party members in a single blow.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

There are plenty of reasons not to like Ruins of Myth Drannor, but I've been enjoying it in spite of them. It's an undemanding RPG that offers simple pleasures. I get ambushed by skeletons, then realize my cleric is perfectly positioned to hit them all with Turn Undead. I meet a weird slug monster, try talking to him and find out he's friendly. I block doors to protect my sorcerer, while rushing enemy spellcasters before they get their big area-of-effect blast off.
It's junk food D&D, but then I mostly play D&D at a table covered in pizza and beer anyway. Between more demanding games, this is an ideal low-stakes guilty pleasure and I'm glad it's finally back.

Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames, Zed Games. He's written for Rock Paper Shotgun, The Big Issue, GamesRadar, Zam, Glixel, Five Out of Ten Magazine, and Playboy.com, whose cheques with the bunny logo made for fun conversations at the bank. Jody's first article for PC Gamer was about the audio of Alien Isolation, published in 2015. Jody edited PC Gamer Indie from 2017 to 2018, and he eventually lived up to his promise to play every Warhammer videogame.

articles.headline: Underkeep class tier list
keyFacts: Destructoid published a class tier list for Underkeep, ranking the game's seven available classes across S-tier, A-tier, and B-tier.
The author stated that S-tier classes like the Warrior, Wizard, and Paladin provide the best impact and ease of use.
A-tier and B-tier classes include the Blood Mage, Ranger, Voidcaller, and Thief, which require specific team builds or patience to succeed.
body: Underkeep offers you six different races and seven different classes to choose from, and you have utmost freedom when finalizing your decisions. All seven classes have their pros and cons, but some of them are better.
In this guide, I will briefly analyze all different classes and rank them across different tiers.
Table of contents
Complete Underkeep class tier list S-tier
A-tier
B-tier
Complete Underkeep class tier list
I have used three different tiers to separate all seven classes available in the game.
S-tier classes are simply the best options due to their in-game impact and ease of use.
A-tier classes will require proper team-building to help them reach their potential.
B-tier classes are decent options as long as you get their class builds on point.
S-tier

Warrior: The Warrior offers the most freedom when it comes to builds. You can do well with any possible setup (as long as it’s relevant to the class). The Warrior can also play multiple roles, which makes him essential for any team.

Wizard: This class can do insane damage once you buff its elemental stacks. The Wizard might not have a lot of health, but it can create barriers to disrupt the enemy. Overall, it’s a great choice as your main DPS.

Paladin: You can’t go wrong with a class that can play as a tank and also provide heals. The Paladin is exceptionally strong against Demons and Undead, and the class works well in plenty of different teams.
A-tier
Blood Mage: Damage wise, the Blood Mage is an S-tier option. However, it’s an extremely difficult class to learn and use, and you’ll need to pair it with the Ranger in a team for maximum synergy.

Ranger: While the Ranger’s damage could be higher, it can mark targets. This makes it easy for its allies to take down enemies faster. More importantly, it doesn’t miss too many shots due to precision.

Voidcaller: Thanks to its healing abilities, the Voidcaller is the premium support class. It can also save teammates with barriers and provide debuffs on the enemy. However, I have found the Paladin to be more effective in my testing.
B-tier
Thief: The thief might be fun to use with its crit and evasion, building it up requires a lot of patience. This class is the most build-reliant out of all options.

articles.headline: Trump declares Alaska Senate race ‘over’ in favor of GOP candidate following ‘Decoy Dan’ scandal
keyFacts: President Trump declared Republican Senator Dan Sullivan the winner of the Alaska Senate race on Truth Social despite a razor-thin margin and outstanding votes.
Trump claimed votes for minor candidates should be attributed to Senator Sullivan, alleging a Democratic ploy involving a decoy candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan.
Alaska election officials continue to count votes, a notoriously slow process that allows up to 15 days for overseas ballots and utilizes ranked-choice voting.
body: President Trump declared the Senate race in Alaska “over” and his favored candidate Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska) the winner — even though the outcome of his race against former Rep. Mary Peltola (D-Alaska) was far from certain.

Trump has previously fumed about the inclusion of “decoy” Daniel J. Sullivan on the ballot, and what he calls a Democratic ploy to draw votes from the senator. He also has urged the Justice Department to investigate.
But on Saturday he went so far as to declare Sen. Sullivan as having “won” the race despite the razor-thin margin and outstanding votes. He was trailing Peltola by fewer than 700 votes.

“Daniel Sullivan is leading substantially in the Alaska Senatorial Race. When you add Daniel (3,600, 1.68%) into Dan, and Gerald Heikes (4,846, 2.27%), Senator Dan Sullivan is up by thousands of Votes. Remember, Heikes was also fraudulently put into the Race,” Trump posted on Truth Social.

“I don’t know what takes so long to announce his win. This should be immediate! Anyone voting for Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr., a man who tried to change his middle initial, but was unable to get it done in time, and who was otherwise nonpolitical – Never even voted – is a vote for Senator Dan Sullivan. The Alaska Race is OVER. Dan Sullivan WON, BY A LOT!” Trump wrote.

Alaska, which covers an expanse of 586,000 square miles, has a notoriously slow counting process. The state allows 10 days from Election Day for votes to arrive and be counted, and 15 days for overseas ballots. It also uses ranked-choice voting, meaning voters whose first-choice candidate loses have their ballot count for their next choice.

Trump on Thursday proposed that Sullivan should also get the votes people cast for minor candidates. “The vote totals for the Fake Dan Sullivan, plus the other ‘slug’ that the Dems put on the Ballot, should be immediately given to the REAL Dan Sullivan, and the Election is over,” he wrote.

A New York Times analysis published Nov. 5 concluded that Sullivan was unlikely to make significant gains through ranked-choice retabulation, since Peltola was actually the second choice of many voters who backed the “decoy” Sullivan. The Times had earlier reported that Peltola’s allies recruited the decoy Sullivan to run.
The latest returns in Alaska showed only 74% of precincts reporting when Trump posted.

articles.headline: Wisconsin state patrol trooper detained by ICE released from custody
keyFacts: Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained and subsequently released Wisconsin state patrol trooper Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe at an airport.
Van Der Merwe has a pending asylum case and work authorization through 2030 to serve in law enforcement, his attorneys stated.
Van Der Merwe must now submit to electronic monitoring, regular check-ins, and an immigration judge hearing, his lawyers said.
body: A Wisconsin state patrol trooper, whom federal immigration agents detained on Thursday at an airport, has been released from their custody.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents approached Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe, a South African national, as he waited to board a domestic flight, according to his law firm Christopher & De León.

Van Der Merwe, who immigrated to the US when he was 14, has been waiting seven years for his asylum case to be heard, his attorneys said in social media posts. In the meantime, he received work authorization, valid through 2030, to serve in Wisconsin’s law enforcement.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) defended Van Der Merwe’s detention in a statement this week, saying he had overstayed a 2019 visa. “Work authorization or a pending application do not confer legal status in the US,” an agency spokesperson told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel.
Van Der Merwe’s lawyers rejected that claim, noting that another DHS agency, US Citizenship and Immigration Services, “authorized him to work”.
“We don’t think ICE even believes its own statement,” the law firm added.
The agency did not immediately respond to an inquiry about what prompted the state trooper’s release.
In a social media update on Friday, Van Der Merwe’s law firm shared that their client would be released, but subject to electronic monitoring and regular check-ins with immigration authorities.
“His release is welcome news. But our fight is not over. Carel will still have to defend his immigration case before an immigration judge,” the attorneys wrote.

“USCIS, an agency within DHS, authorized Carel to work. He used that authorization to serve and protect Wisconsin communities. ICE, another agency within DHS, then detained him. DHS owes this family more than silence,” they continued.
Video of Van Der Merwe’s graduation ceremony last year showed that his badge was pinned on by his father in front of Wisconsin’s governor.

Van Der Merwe’s family of white South Africans arrived during Donald Trump’s first term, but they had good reason to expect that they would be granted asylum after Trump returned to office last year and signed an executive order saying the US would “promote the resettlement of Afrikaner refugees”, based on the false claim that they would be “escaping government-sponsored race-based discrimination” at home.

In addition to a series of highly public, contentious and in some cases deadly ICE raids across several US cities, the Trump administration’s mass deportation agenda has played out more furtively at domestic and international airports. Travelers with visas, green-card holders and pending asylum cases have been detained in what some experts say is an effort to meet arrest quotas imposed on the agency by the White House.
Van Der Merwe’s law firm advised noncitizens with unresolved immigration paperwork to consult immigration attorneys before traveling by air.
“Even if you have flown without problems before, do not assume the same will happen now,” they said.

articles.headline: Raspberry Pi 5 price hike means the 16GB model now costs three times what it did at launch — and of course, the global RAM shortage is to blame
keyFacts: Raspberry Pi raised the 16GB Raspberry Pi 5 price by $80 to $385, which is more than triple its $120 launch price.
Company CEO Eben Upton attributed the price hike to a lack of alternative 16GB DRAM supply and wider component shortages.
Raspberry Pi called the price increases temporary, but memory makers expect tight supply to last until 2028 or 2030.
body: - Raspberry Pi has raised the 16GB Pi 5's price by $80 to $385, more than triple its $120 launch price
- Company CEO blames lack of alternative 16GB DRAM supply, compounded by wider component shortages
- Raspberry Pi called the hikes temporary, but memory makers expect tight supply to last until 2028 to 2030
Raspberry Pi has raised the price of its 16GB Raspberry Pi 5 yet again, and the flagship board now sits far from the brand's budget roots.
In a blog post, company CEO Eben Upton confirmed an $80 increase that takes the board to $385, which is more than triple the $120 it cost at launch in January 2025.
The 16GB variants of Compute Module 5 increase by $40 in the same round, while the Raspberry Pi 500+, the company's keyboard computer that also offers 16GB of RAM, remains at its existing price.
A far-reaching memory crisis dictates prices

The threefold figure is cumulative rather than a single jump: The November 2026 increase on its own amounts to roughly 26%, but the rest built up over a run of rises that began in December 2025, when the 16GB Pi 5 went from $120 to $145. February added $60, leaving the board 70% more expensive than at launch, and April added a further $100.

That April 2026 round also brought a new 3GB Raspberry Pi 4, introduced to give buyers a cheaper middle option, with Upton saying at the time that the LPDDR4 memory used in the Pi 4 and Pi 5 had risen sevenfold in price over the previous year.

November's change also comes barely a month after Raspberry Pi raised prices on its 2GB boards by $12.50 each, having decided that shielding those models from earlier price increases was no longer sustainable.

Upton's explanation is more specific than a general complaint about RAM prices. He blamed "a lack of alternative supply for 16GB DRAM, compounded by other ongoing component shortages," which suggests the bottleneck is sourcing at that particular density rather than cost alone.

Raspberry Pi, for its part, has been qualifying additional memory suppliers through 2026 to widen its options, and the wording implies those alternatives remain thinnest at the top of the range.

Interestingly, despite the price increases, demand hasn't fallen but rather grown considerably. Direct sales of the Pi 5 rose 47% in the half, and Raspberry Pi says demand for the 8GB variants continued to grow despite higher prices.
For buyers, the new pricing produces some odd comparisons. The 8GB Raspberry Pi 5 lists at $175, which means the extra 8GB on the 16GB model now costs $210, more than an entire 8GB board.

The spared-but-similarly-specced Pi 500+ sharpens the point. For $25 more than the bare 16GB board, it pairs the same processor and memory with a 256GB NVMe SSD and a mechanical keyboard. It's no substitute for embedded projects that need the bare board's footprint, but for desktop use, the standalone 16GB Pi 5 is now difficult to justify once one considers the cost of a standalone SSD alone, even if the keyboard is considered a non-factor.

Buying a cheaper board and upgrading it isn't a workaround either, since Raspberry Pi firmware locks boards to the memory capacity they shipped with. For those who don't need 16GB at all, we have found that an 8GB starter kit can often be a better buy than the board on its own.

Upton's own advice is to avoid paying for memory you don't need by choosing lower-density variants or older models, or by optimizing applications. He also warned that some sellers are exploiting the shortage by inflating prices or misrepresenting products, and urged buyers to stick to approved resellers.
A "temporary" crisis might be an understatement
Raspberry Pi continues to describe the memory squeeze as temporary and says it intends to roll back its increases once costs fall. Its own definition of temporary is fairly elastic, though.

In the company's September results, Upton described the current cycle as "a large, but ultimately typical, instance of a phenomenon that periodically affects the industry," with meaningful new supply not expected until 2028.

Memory makers are gloomier still. SK Hynix titled a section of its third-quarter results "Memory supply shortage to persist through 2030," and Micron has warned that shortages could run into 2028 or beyond.

TrendForce, whose latest outlook Upton linked in his post, expects DRAM suppliers to keep prioritizing server products through the fourth quarter, leaving the wider market undersupplied even as contract prices rise slowly.

The entry-level boards, however, remain a bright spot, with the 1GB Pi 4 and Pi 5 still at $35 and $45, respectively. Rising prices risk putting the Pi out of reach of schools and kids, and for now the bottom of the range is still holding the line. At the top, though, the 16GB Pi 5 has become a premium product by necessity rather than design, and the CEO's optimism might not be shared by many consumers in the market for one in the near future.

articles.headline: Echoes of Mirror's Edge, Dishonored and a dream set in Italy I once had can be found in Boars in Rome, an expressive parkour platformer set in dystopian Rome
keyFacts: Developer Benji Savage announced Boars in Rome, an expressive parkour platformer set in a dystopian version of Rome.
The Steam page states that players explore abandoned Earth remnants where historical monuments mix with futurist megastructures after being frozen in time.
The game currently has no release date, but a playtest is available for users to sign up and access immediately on Steam.
body: Years ago, I had this dream where I was parkouring through a greatly sunken version of Venice, no doubt sourced from the many hours I put into Assassin's Creed 2 as a teen who should have been studying for their GCSEs a lot more than they were. It's stuck with me after all this time mostly because of how much I wanted to capture that feeling again somehow, as the real Assassin's Creed didn't quite cut it. And lo and behold, there I was today browsing Bluesky when I came across Boars in Rome, a Mirror's Edge and Counter Strike Surf inspired parkour platformer set in a dystopian version of Rome.

Truthfully, witnessing the clip I've shared below was baffling to me. "This is what I dreamt of!" More or less, anyway, for the setting isn't quite the same; "You have been selected to start a new life off planet. Earth has been abandoned," explains the game's Steam page. "Machines keep working and nature claims what remains. Find out what happened while you were frozen in time by exploring the remnants of Rome where historical monuments mix with futurist megastructures."
Mirrors Edge x Counter Strike Surf where you parkour on anything!
Be smooth n stylish in dystopian Rome. Or just jump around and explore, whatever works for you.
It's called Boars in Rome!
#PitchYaGame
[image or embed]
— Benji Savage (@ceplok.bsky.social) November 6, 2026 at 12:05 PM

Not all of it matches that dream of mine, some of it leans much more into brutalism than the typical, much older architecture you'd expect of Rome, but it's there nonetheless. In motion, Boars in Rome feels quite oneiric too. There is so much more control over the game's avatar than what my real body is capable of, or wants to do. You can run, jump, slide and wallrun, positioning it quite closely to VHOLUME mechanically. Where it differs is in its additives, movement tech like being able to swing on lampposts or vault over low down obstacles.

VHOLUME is more of a game about providing you with a simple toolkit and leaving you to push it to its maximum. Boars in Roam is a touch more expressive, and I'd dare to even call it an immersive sim. The levels you can romp around are linear, you have an end point to reach, only the journey is up to you. It certainly feels appropriate to put it in the im sim camp given that, at least the game's first level, calls to mind Viktor Antonov's work on Dishonored (and Half-Life 2, too, honestly).

As it currently stands, there's no release date for Boars in Rome, but there is a playtest you can sign up and gain immediate access to if you fancy a go yourself; you can do so on Steam right here, or at least pop it a wishlist.

articles.headline: Wendy’s Just Released a Video Game Where You Can Win Fast Food
keyFacts: Wendy’s released a free mobile and desktop role-playing video game called WendyQuest on Nov. 4.
Players aged 18 and older in the US can win codes in the game to redeem for menu items with a purchase.
A Wendy’s spokesperson said WendyQuest is the brand's first fully owned video game after previous gaming culture involvement.
body: Wendy’s has turned its red-headed mascot into a wisecracking warrior who battles evil french fry robots in a free mobile game called WendyQuest. The company announced the retro-style role-playing game on Nov. 4. The announcement came with a promotion where you can win codes in the game, which are redeemable for menu items like fries and burgers at Wendy’s locations.

WendyQuest is available to download on iOS and Android. Desktop users can get it through the Steam platform. Anyone can play the game, but the promotion is restricted to people who are 18 and up living in the US.
You need to sign up for a Wendy’s account to redeem a code. While the food you can win is free, it requires you to buy something when you go.
More from CNET
“Wendy’s has been a part of gaming culture for years, including on Twitch, Fortnite and Feast of Legends, but WendyQuest is the brand’s first fully owned video game,” a spokesperson for Wendy’s said.
Fast-food quest

I downloaded WendyQuest, and my daughter and I played it for a while. The blocky graphics are reminiscent of the home-console video games of the late 1980s and early 1990s. It plays a lot like a simplified version of the DragonQuest, Final Fantasy and Breath of Fire games from the era, only stuffed with fast-food branding.

Rather than the regular turn-based battles that come standard in the early RPGs, this game adds a timing element, where you need to press a button at the right time like you do in old golfing video games.

It’s not a bad game. The light humor is suitable for younger players, and it’s fun to play. Like many RPGs, you battle monsters to gain levels, search around the maps for hidden areas, buy items and talk to people in towns to figure out what’s going on.

It took us over an hour to complete the first region, Fryshire, and get the Fry Stone, which unlocks a promo code for medium fries, free with a purchase. But again, you have to sign up for a Wendy’s account on their website or on the company’s mobile app.
Winning prizes

Video games have a long history of offering real-world prizes to players as promotions. Swordquest, a series of video games released in the early 1980s for the Atari 2600, famously held a contest where players tried to win actual treasure made of gold and jewels.

In 2015, a promotion for the video game Just Cause 3 offered players the chance to win a private island. Developer Square Enix clarified that it couldn’t guarantee that the island would be livable and that the winner would have to pay all the taxes involved.
The reward codes from WendyQuest expire seven days after you get them, and Wendy’s says the codes are first come, first served.

articles.headline: Rubio defends Trump’s Iran decision: ‘Elected to do the hard things’
keyFacts: Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended President Donald Trump's decision to initiate the conflict in Iran during a Friday night speech at Mar-a-Lago.
Rubio stated that Trump was elected to do hard things and that the military action was necessary to prevent Iran from obtaining a weapon of mass destruction.
The defense follows significant Republican losses in recent midterm elections, where Democrats overperformed amid public disapproval of the Iran conflict.
body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended President Donald Trump’s decision to initiate the conflict in Iran at an event on Friday night.

While speaking at the Mar-a-Lago resort in Palm Beach, Florida , Rubio offered his post-midterm-election assessment of the conflict a few days after Vice President JD Vance issued a lengthy statement following the Republican Party’s significant losses. Vance directly addressed the monthslong conflict and “the cost of living/inflation,” saying Democrats’ election success was largely tied to the situation in Iran and that voters frustrated by the result should focus on “electing Republicans who share your worldview.” Trump backed Vance’s statement by saying it was “largely true.”

Rubio perspective was markedly more complimentary of Trump’s February decision and the president himself, as the secretary said he “sees firsthand every single day” that Trump’s first priority is serving the people.
Secretary of State @marcorubio speaks at CPAC Mar-a-Lago pic.twitter.com/PTGMJcZyMv
— CPAC (@CPAC) November 7, 2026

“The most important thing the president can do for our country is to keep it safe,” he said. “And there are people around the world that want to destroy it. They want to destroy our country; they want to destroy our way of life. He was elected to do the hard things… it would have been very easy to do what multiple presidents before him have done, which is ignore the Iran thing, leave it for the next guy, put it aside, and don’t worry about it. That would have been the easiest thing to do.”

“But this president didn’t do that… we cannot live in a world in which the most radical, terroristic regime on the planet possesses a weapon of mass destruction,” Rubio continued. “And we had president after president ignore it and allow it to linger, but this president wasn’t elected to ignore it, and he wasn’t elected to allow threats to linger.” Though the public largely doesn’t approve of the conflict, according to public polling, the White House has defended it by saying it was necessary to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, and that further degrading its military will disrupt the terrorist-sponsoring nation’s regional activities and ability to threaten the United States.
BYRON YORK: IN THE GOP, A NEW 2028 RACE

Trump’s approval rating has steadily declined since he took office in January 2025, while that of the broader Democratic Party has remained roughly the same during the same period. Democrats nonetheless dealt Republicans a striking defeat this week, as they won essentially every race deemed critical in the lead-up to the elections and significantly overperformed in traditionally red states such as Texas.

Debates about the 2028 presidential election have come into focus since. Both Vance and Rubio have long been floated as potential candidates, and by extension, heirs to Trump and the current administration. Neither candidate has yet declared they will run.

articles.headline: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 to draw level with La Liga leaders Barcelona
keyFacts: Real Madrid defeated Valencia 3-0 on Saturday with goals from Federico Valverde, Arda Guler, and Kylian Mbappe.
The victory moved Real Madrid provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona.
Valencia finished the match with 10 men after Jose Gaya was sent off for a late foul near the end of the game.
body: Kylian Mbappe scored for the seventh match running as Real Madrid pulled provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a 3-0 win at 10-man Valencia.
Reigning champions Barca visit Atletico Madrid, third, on Sunday, aiming to move back clear of the chasing pack.
Jose Mourinho’s Madrid largely dominated at Mestalla Stadium on Saturday, securing an eighth win in a row across all competitions.
Federico Valverde and Arda Guler’s first-half goals put Madrid in the driving seat, and Mbappe added a third in the second half.
Los Blancos were without winger Vinicius Junior, who was serving the final game of a four-match ban.
Madrid have thrived in his absence, putting heavy pressure on Barca, whom they beat in the Camp Nou Clasico on October 25.
In the ninth minute, the match stopped for players and fans to pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who tragically died on Tuesday.
Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made a smart save to deny Aaron Mayol, who had picked Aurelien Tchouameni’s pocket in a dangerous area.
Valencia’s Guido Rodriguez had a goal disallowed for offside before Mourinho’s side took control.
Valverde drilled Madrid ahead from outside the area after Mbappe’s free kick was blocked by the Valencia wall and fell to the Uruguayan.
Guler soon doubled the lead after Jude Bellingham’s cross was deflected kindly into his path.
Guler had a good chance for the third early in the second half, but Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski grabbed the ball as the midfielder tried to round him.
Minutes later, Dimitrievski saved well from Mbappe, as the French striker ran through and tried to dink the ball over him.
Bellingham powered through the defence and was also denied by the goalkeeper, as was Mbappe, who followed up with an overhead kick, as Madrid tried to find a third to kill off the game.
Eventually, Mbappe produced it, bursting onto a dangerous pass by Guler to dart past Dimitrievski and squeeze home his 13th league goal of the campaign.
It was the forward’s 17th goal in 16 games across all competitions. Mbappe has netted in his last seven appearances for Madrid.
Valencia’s Jose Gaya was dismissed with about 10 minutes remaining for a late sliding foul on Mbappe to further spoil Javier Aguirre’s team’s night.
Earlier, new Espanyol coach Eder Sarabia’s side were held to a goalless home draw by Deportivo A Coruna.
Osasuna snatched a late 1-1 draw against Athletic Bilbao, while Racing Santander came from behind to beat Malaga 2-1.

articles.headline: For This Year’s N7 Day, Fans, Alumni And Policy Makers Fought For Mass Effect’s Future
keyFacts: Fans, developers, and policy makers marked N7 Day by pushing to save the Mass Effect series following EA's closure of BioWare.
Supporters launched a campaign featuring Times Square ads, billboard trucks, and a video statement from composer Sam Hulick and the game's cast.
Canadian New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis and MP Don Davies expressed frustration over the closure and supported the petition.
body: Fourteen years ago, BioWare designated November 7th as N7 Day. Originally a commemoration for the original Mass Effectâs fifth anniversary, this yearâs festivities have become something of a funeral, with fans, developers, performers and even policy makers in attendance. Following the sudden closure of BioWare last month, and the subsequent materials about Mass Effect Universe that have surfaced, players are intensifying their push to do the series justice.
Today is a very special day for Mass Effect fans.
We've worked incredibly hard to bring together most of the original Mass Effect trilogy's voice cast to share a very important message with you.
We need to #SaveMassEffect. pic.twitter.com/FOp0qp4wBI
— We are Mass Effect – #SaveMassEffect (@WeAreMassEffect) November 7, 2026

âThe hardworking people who made Mass Effect deserve to see their vision through,â says Mass Effect composer Sam Hulick, joined by much of the gameâs cast in a video statement. âIâm not ready to see the story end either.â

After years of quiet and conflict with the parent company, EA announced the unceremonious closure of BioWare, creators of Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and more. It comes amid a controversial acquisition of EA from a consortium of private equity holders, including the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund and Jared Kushnerâs Affinity Partners. Adding insult to injury, the shuttering dropped just a few weeks before N7 day, which in the past had fans awaiting for any news regarding the Mass Effect series. Obviously, no one was on standby for such a party this year, even though evidence suggests EA had already brought decorations. Instead, incensed stalwarts took the opportunity to intensify their campaign to save the series.

After purchasing ad space in Times Square, more billboards and trucks for the “Save Mass Effect” movement have emerged in Wales, Texas, California and Edmonton, the latter being BioWareâs stomping grounds. On top of the series’ own alumni, various other developers and voice performers have joined in. Five Nights At Freddyâs Kellen Goff shared his thoughts on the importance of the series and the movementâs efforts thus far. Owlcat Games released their own video reminiscing on the series, having just hired Dragon Age writer David Gaider to work on Osiris Reborn, their own RPG based on the sci-fi series The Expanse.

One of the more unexpected fronts of support come from Canadaâs New Democratic Party. Newly elected party leader Avi Lewis expressed his frustrations with EA and private equity when the closure was first announced, suggesting stronger policy to protect Canadian businesses and even suggesting the federal government intervene in BioWareâs future. While there already is plenty of Canadian funding wrapped up in the gaming industry (see: Ubisoft), NDP member of parliament Don Davies boosted support for the petition, as well as photoshopping his head on Commander Sheppard.

BioWare is an Edmonton-based video game studio that created acclaimed series like #MassEffect, Baldurâs Gate, and Dragon Age. Canadaâs video game industry creates some of our most important cultural exports, and #BioWare was among our greatest success stories. (1/3) pic.twitter.com/KeL6LeRzuW
— Don Davies (@DonDavies) November 6, 2026

The major front for N7 day appears to be Mass Effect itself. If the petition signatures arenât convincing, theyâre hoping for a high count of simultaneous players on the original game will make a stronger case. Regardless of what course correction is even possible at this point, fans are making themselves unignorable, as billboard trucks roam outside of EAâs Redwood headquarters, Madrid offices are tagged and the announcement of massive back catalogue restoration, which would have been really cool if not for everything else, is drowned out by commenters.

articles.headline: After the midterms, things are looking rocky for Elon Musk and data centers
keyFacts: Voters rejected multiple data center ballot measures and elected politicians who campaigned on restricting data centers during the midterm elections.
Tech analysts said Elon Musk gained little from his political donations while his companies are now headquartered in a heavily Democratic state.
Companies like OpenAI are changing policies to remove nondisclosure agreements and rebrand data centers as compute campuses following the election results.
body: Democrats’ historic victory in this week’s midterm elections could also have a dramatic effect on the tech industry.

In dozens of local ballot measures, voters rejected data centers. And even when they weren’t voting on the issue directly, they were electing politicians — like Texas’ new governor-elect Gina Hinojosa — who campaigned on the promise of restricting data centers.

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed what the midterms mean for the tech industry. Sean kicked it off by noting that Elon Musk “seems to have basically nothing out of donating half a billion dollars” to Republicans, while his companies are now headquartered “in a state that has, remarkably, turned about as blue as it could possibly turn.”

And Kirsten said that while data centers probably weren’t the main cause of the “blue wave,” they’ve become an “an increasingly grassroots issue, in part because of how hyperscalers and companies have gone about” getting their projects approved. And now, “we’re already seeing companies like OpenAI all of a sudden go, ‘Actually, we can change our policies.’”
Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity.

Sean O’Kane: First off, let’s talk about the fact that one of the biggest data center builders was also the largest donor to the Republican Party. Elon Musk seems to have gotten basically nothing out of donating half a billion dollars — maybe even more, by the time we see the final count — and in fact is now sitting there with all of his businesses in a state that has, remarkably, turned about as blue as it could possibly turn for the first time in a very long time, if ever.

That, I think, is the biggest thing hanging above a lot of this discussion. But, there were also a bunch of ballot measures up around the country that would have paved the way for data centers to get built faster. Almost all of them got shot down, or voted against. [Actually, many of the ballot measures would have imposed restrictions or moratoriums on data centers, and almost all of those measures passed.]

With [Democrats] in power, there is a consensus view, at least in the tech world, that this is going to mean we have a lot of roadblocks ahead for data centers, especially in places like Texas, where [you have] folks like the governor-elect [Gina] Hinojosa, who has spoken pretty openly about this being a campaign promise and something that she wants to focus on once she takes power, now that she’s beaten Greg Abbott.
It’s the thing that I think the tech world is maybe a little too focused on. I’m curious what you guys think about that.

Anthony Ha: I don’t necessarily think that they’re too focused on it, but I understand why it would feel a little bit disproportionate — the data center ballot measures, certainly there were a number of them, but it wasn’t something that was on the ballot everywhere.

And in different races, the dynamic might have been a bit different, but there was this undercurrent and sense that it seems to be an issue that reaches across the country, that is bipartisan in a lot of ways, but that the Democrats seem to have been more effective at harnessing that energy. And of course, there’s all kinds of reasons why the Democrats did so well on Tuesday, but it does seem like anti-AI and especially anti-data center sentiment was a big part of it. That seems like a pretty potent political force.

The next two years, [and] potentially beyond that, are going to be more difficult for tech companies in general, and hyperscalers, data center companies in particular. I also imagine that they have to be a little bit worried about: Is this going to continue to be an issue, not just with the people who got elected this year, but potentially in 2028 and beyond?

Kirsten Korosec: Absolutely. I don’t think that the data center issue is what brought everyone to the polls and led to the quote-unquote “blue wave.” However, I will say that data centers have been an increasingly grassroots issue, in part because of how hyperscalers and companies have gone about getting these data centers [approved] — very secretive, oftentimes requiring NDAs of a elected officials or appointed officials, not sharing information about the scale of a project in very environmentally sensitive areas, including in the Southwest, where there’s very much a water scarcity issue.
So I think that a lot of folks — Republicans, independents, and Democrats — all saw this as wrong. They were motivated by it, but I don’t think it was a singular issue.

Now, here’s the interesting thing. There was a lot of waving of hands about how [AI companies] can’t possibly operate under any other circumstances. And we’re already seeing companies like OpenAI all of a sudden go, “Actually, we can change our policies.” They just released what they call a compute campus policy blueprint. And guess what? They’re not going to require NDAs anymore. They’re going to share their plans and supposedly operate in less secrecy.

I think what this shows is that when you put up either a regulatory certainty in the marketplace, or at least signals of going in that direction, then corporations will respond. If you don’t do that, they will not necessarily do the thing that we hope that they will do.

Anthony: One thing I want to emphasize is that they’re calling it this [their] “compute campus policy.” And part of what that’s doing, beyond laying out these policy changes, is also an attempt to rebrand data centers, because they have become such a toxic phrase. So they’re not data centers anymore, they are compute campuses, and I’m curious, whether either of you think that’ll take.

Sean: I mean, this is ridiculous. Come on. It’s not going to change anything. It’s going to cause them more effort. For a company that likes to say that it’s no longer focused on side quests, OpenAI still loves to go in different directions a lot. And this is just the latest kind of thing where it’s just like: Why are you spending time on this at all? It doesn’t really seem like it’s going to move the needle.

Kirsten: I have a great idea for OpenAI. Because in the spirit of making threatening things seem cute, they should 100% create a compute campuses avatar, [a] cutesy thing, and then just present that instead of a power-, energy-sucking, water-sucking data center.
Anthony: And if these are just lovely compute campuses, they should just build their own offices there or work next door, see how that works out for them.

Something else that I’m wondering about is, to what extent the election is maybe the second part of a one-two punch. [We’ve just seen] a big shift in how Wall Street is reacting to a lot of these hyperscalers and AI companies and this sense that [investors] are not excited about the idea that they should be spending all this money building new data centers, spending all this money on compute. And so there’s a financial incentive not to build all these data centers.

I’m very curious how that’s going to play out. [From a regulatory standpoint,] it’s probably going to be harder to build data centers. Wall Street is probably not going to reward you for building data centers. But at the same time, to get to the scale that they want to get to, they are probably going to need to build data centers somewhere.
